amira: Heads-up: customers hitting a TS inference mismatch when using the SDK from Edge bundles. ESM install gives proper generics, CJS install turns them into unknown/any.

amira: Short repro: our `invoke<T>(opts: InvokeOpts<T>): Promise<Result<T>>` overload works with ESM build but not with CJS consumers (webpack/older Node setups).

derek: Do we publish separate .d.ts files for `exports.import` vs `exports.require`? If so they might have different overload ordering.

amira: Yes: dist/esm/index.d.ts has generic-first; dist/cjs/index.d.ts lists the broad fallback before the generic. TS picks the first matching overload -> inference lost.

zoe: Two quick fixes: 1) canonicalize to a single .d.ts referenced by both entrypoints; 2) add a CI consumer-pack test that installs the tarball in both ESM and CJS tiny projects and runs `tsc --noEmit`.

derek: Also add a post-dts check (tiny TS API script) to assert that for each overloaded function the more specific/generic signature appears before the fallback. Add the check to pack step.

amira: For the short term we won't change public types to `any`. We'll reorder overload emission and ship a patch. Also add dev docs recommending `moduleResolution: node16` / `esModuleInterop` guidance for customers who still use old bundlers.

packager-bot: Created issue #4410 "CJS/ESM .d.ts overload ordering causes generic inference regressions" and attached sample artifacts.

amira: I'll open a PR with the failing consumer test and the dts canonicalization. Thanks!
